original_card.question: Can a new local cost interface change the deficit-to-recursive-cost ratio beyond current packing?
methods: Propose a changed helper inventory and derive an optimistic exact moment.
Design a small completed instance and independently verify its endpoint and rank bill.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A new physically realizable contract outside the frozen catalogue whose per-call profile, screened with ceiling.ceiling(), beats the selected word's packing ceiling; a lower cap does not establish identical circuitry or order attainable optima, and is insufficient to pass the stronger-budget target under this model. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read the selected word's per-call local profile, its packing ceiling and the lever table; run levers.py for the ideal budget of the lever you target.
first_step.scope: Positive control and planning budget only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Before any synthesis, write the candidate per-call local profile (and centre charge / unpaid coordinates if changed) and screen it with ceiling.ceiling(); reject it if even the ideal ceiling does not beat the selected word's by your stated margin.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Packing of the selected word is capped at +0.87% (ceiling model); only a lower local excess spend or a changed coverage law raises the cap.
allowed_variations: Narrow to one changed boundary or helper type with explicit counts.
If the coverage law, template or guard changes, derive an applicable fully charged replacement bound instead of applying the incumbent ceiling outside its scope.
scope_change_triggers: Mixing only providers already inside the pinned catalogue.
Only changing helper terminal subspaces and monotone frames within the fixed scalar word, entrances and cleanup contract already covered by #1995/#2013.

Continuing a partial cost improvement while leaving the same unpriced consumer, restoration or central-readout obligation unresolved; refresh the family expansion decision first. Local product-retiming evidence has a narrow scope and is not a ban on changed graphs or contracts.

actual_scope: On PR #3042's two six-skip provider words (also PR #3054's words): the complete class of exact restore-only rewrites (A with its prelude, B, warps, cut, initial corrections, precondition, compensation, start frames, helper end frames, removed helpers and buffers fixed; any restore scalar gate sequence; all frames re-solved; exactness = PR2833's auditor), priced by the certified frame solver at b = 0.001703676387993676.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a changed local cost interface can beat current packing. On the six-skip words the only lever left to restore edits is the local frame bill at fixed widths and buffers, and PR3057/PR3065 already settled the fixed-scalar-order frame problem. This package narrows the card to one word pair and one section (the restore) but widens the move set to every exact restore gate sequence, and proves that the published restore is optimal there; a scoped negative that tells the next construction which premise (A/B or the target interface) must change.
bottleneck_link: The restore-phase overhead of PR3042's words over the unconstrained empty-restore optimum is 499,481 units per call (161,558 forced entry caps on A/B chains + 337,923 forced visits). All of it is forced by A/B and the restored helpers' required content, so no restore-only rewrite can lower the local profile or raise the inventory's packing cap; a gain must change A/B or the target interface.
stop_rule: Stop at an exact lower bound equal to the certified cost on both providers (scoped negative, no dependent construction round), or at the first exact restore-only rewrite that beats it (then one complete release). The bound must be calibrated on PR2979's words, where it has to reproduce dcharb78's realized 29,976.
evidence: run_registered.py (Python 3.12 standard library): MANIFEST/PINS; verify.py (exact frame optimum, restore-entry rows and their rank, forced coordinates, 88 caps, LB_forced 10,867,765,164, classification 42 blocked + 9 payer groups = 337,923, bound = certified cost 10,868,103,087 on both providers, 51 literal visits all charged, normal-45 facts, PR2979 calibration gap 29,976 = the six PR3042 skips, per-block erratum of PR3042's README, auditor-semantics controls, PR3056/PR3060 attainment controls, 12 rejection controls) and census.py (complete deletion census, re-derived tail-exchange candidate list with sampled re-checks); regenerated receipts byte-equal to certificates/; lane K's stored receipts and its current bound.py/lbforced.py cross-checked in evidence/laneK/.

open_questions.question: Can an A-phase (input block) or B-phase re-synthesis lower the restore's forced overhead (161,558 forced-cap units on A/B chains; 192,384 units of kernel/preload visits in 30 registers)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: This package proves the whole 499,481-unit restore overhead forced at fixed A/B; any further local gain on these words must change A/B, i.e. the forced coordinates M of the restored helpers or the entry bounds L/U.
open_questions.first_step: For a candidate A/B block, recompute the restore-entry rows, M, the caps and restore_bound.bound on the edited word before pricing it; only candidates whose bound falls below the current cost are worth realizing.
open_questions.blocked_by: Lane K's single-move A/B censuses scored by this bound (local evidence) found no positive gap; multi-gate input-block re-synthesis needs exact dirty-input identities for the changed block and its frame bill.
